turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero on Owen's essay, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Let's pick up where we were.
We were at my question, Hale, and you haven't answered it. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
Earlier you admitted Owen used ChatGPT for the first paragraph.
I said no such thing, and you'll notice you can't quote me. If you have something that shows Owen used anything, put it in front of me. Otherwise, who decided on the zero?
And you agreed a minute ago that the zero is fair.
I haven't agreed to anything, and the zero is not fair. It comes off, and you can put in writing who decided it and why nobody called me first.
You also said Claire cheated four years ago. Your words.
I never said that, and Claire won her appeal. Be very careful with your next sentence. I'm taking this to the principal's office when we're done.
You said you'd accept the zero if I kept it off his record. I wrote it down.
Then read it to me, because I never said that. The zero comes off, and nothing goes on his record either way. What else do you have, besides things I supposedly said?
Okay, so we agree then. Great.
We agree on nothing. The zero comes off, you apologise for how Owen found out, and until I see a document, I'm going upstairs.
